sections.label: Overview
sections.summary: The Knot presents a consistent wedding-planning brand with strong visual identity and clear audience focus on engaged couples.

readout.brand_system: Marketplace-first brand with warm visual language anchored in gold and blush tones.
readout.main_risk: Category positioning overlaps with Zola and The Bash without clear differentiation.
readout.decisions_needed: The brand team needs to decide whether to lead with marketplace utility or emotional aspiration.

sections.label: Strategy
sections.summary: Positioning centers on trusted all-in-one planning with strong vendor network depth.

sections.label: Language
sections.summary: Voice is warm and aspirational but inconsistent across channels.

sections.label: Personas
sections.summary: Engaged couple persona is implicit across assets but not formally documented.

sections.label: Audiences
sections.summary: Primary audience consistently targeted across paid and organic.

sections.label: Market
sections.summary: No competitive landscape document; analysis reconstructed from public signals only.

sections.label: Proof
sections.summary: Testimonials and vendor reviews are plentiful; editorial awards provide credibility.

sections.label: Design
sections.summary: Visual identity is well-documented with consistent typography and palette.

open_questions.question: Is the primary competitive alternative The Bash or Zola?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Category frame depends on which competitor is the true alternative-of-record. Getting this wrong misaligns all downstream messaging.

open_questions.question: Which tone register — warm-aspirational or practical-utility — should lead on product pages?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Voice inconsistency between homepage and email creates trust gaps at acquisition.

open_questions.question: Is the primary persona the first-time bride or the co-planning couple?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Photography direction and copy hierarchy diverge depending on which persona leads.

open_questions.question: What market category does The Knot own — 'wedding planning' or 'wedding marketplace'?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Category choice determines search posture and controls which competitors are foregrounded.

open_questions.question: Are editorial awards being actively promoted or quietly deprecated?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Proof hierarchy needs to be consistent. Mixing evergreen and time-limited proof creates inconsistent credibility signals.

open_questions.question: Is the gold-and-blush palette scoped to wedding surfaces only or intended to span all verticals?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Palette scope affects vendor-facing products and any market extensions the brand team is considering.
